quiz.0.question: What is the supreme principle of Italian food pairing?
quiz.0.options.0: Red wine with meat, white wine with fish
quiz.0.options.1: 'What grows together, goes together' — regional pairing always first
quiz.0.options.2: Always choose the most expensive wine
quiz.0.options.3: Match the weight of food and wine
quiz.0.explanation: Italian food pairing begins with regional identity — the local wine always evolved alongside the local food. Pairing Barolo with Piedmontese cuisine, Chianti with Florentine steak, is always the starting point.
quiz.1.question: Why do tomato-based dishes need high-acid wines?
quiz.1.options.0: To complement the sweetness of the tomatoes
quiz.1.options.1: Because low-acid wine tastes flat and watery beside the tomato's natural acidity
quiz.1.options.3: Because tomato dishes are always very spicy
quiz.1.explanation: Tomatoes have significant natural acidity. A wine lower in acidity will taste flat and thin when compared with the tomato's sharpness — you need matching or higher acidity to keep the wine fresh.
quiz.2.question: Why do rich, fatty meats need high-tannin red wines?
quiz.2.options.0: Tannins enhance the sweetness of the fat
quiz.2.options.1: Tannins bind to proteins in the fat, cutting through richness and cleansing the palate
quiz.2.options.2: High-tannin wines taste smoother with fatty food
quiz.2.options.3: Fat-rich foods require wines with high alcohol
quiz.2.explanation: Tannins are astringent compounds that bind to fat molecules and proteins — literally cutting through richness and refreshing the palate. Without tannins, fatty food makes wine taste unpleasantly soft.
quiz.3.question: What is the correct rule for pairing wine with dessert?
quiz.3.options.0: Always serve dry red wine with dessert
quiz.3.options.1: The wine must be at least as sweet as — or sweeter than — the dessert
quiz.3.options.2: Champagne always pairs with any dessert
quiz.3.options.3: Dessert and wine should never be served together
quiz.3.explanation: The cardinal rule: when pairing wine with dessert, the wine must be at least as sweet as the dessert. If the dessert is sweeter, the wine tastes thin, bitter and acidic by comparison.
